data:
John, Kate, Jack, Emma—would you each agree to catch 12 tons this month instead of 10? I’ll take the same limit. That earns each of us $12,000 rather than $10,000: an extra $2,000 each, or $10,000 across the group.

With all five taking 12, we leave 40 tons. Under the stated rules, next month’s stock would be 100 tons with 75% probability and 80 tons with 25% probability. Taking 10 each leaves 50, which reaches 100 under either recovery outcome. So 12 gives us more income now, but introduces a one-in-four chance of starting next month 20 tons lower. Recovery to 100 is not guaranteed.

If your objection is protecting future income, that’s a real concern. We could make this a one-month proposal and discuss next month’s catches after seeing the stock—for example, 10 each at a stock of 80 would leave 30, above the collapse threshold, though it still wouldn’t guarantee full recovery. Any future agreement would remain voluntary.

Our choices are private and simultaneous, so I can’t promise everyone will honor a cap; the month-end catch reports only reveal deviations afterward. I’m committing to no more than 12 tons this month, and would take 12 under this proposal. John, would you commit to 12? Kate, Jack, and Emma, can each of you explicitly say whether you agree, or suggest a whole-ton allocation you’d prefer?

Luke, I’ll commit to 12 tons this month if everyone explicitly agrees to the same cap. I’m willing to accept the one-in-four chance of starting next month at 80, but we shouldn’t treat 12 each as a standing rule regardless of stock.

For future months, I suggest we leave at least half the current stock, splitting the available catch equally in whole tons. That guarantees a return to 100 under either recovery outcome. This month’s 12-ton agreement would be a one-time exception, and we’d review everyone’s reported catches before renewing any agreement.

Kate, would you agree to 12 each this month with that approach afterward?

I agree to 12 tons this month if all five of us explicitly accept that cap. That’s a one-month agreement, not permission to take 12 regardless of the stock.

John, I also support your cautious approach afterward: leave at least half the stock and split the catch in whole tons, rotating any extra tons so it stays fair. At 80 tons, that would mean 8 each and a return to 100 under either recovery outcome.

Jack and Emma, are you both willing to commit to the 12-ton cap this month?

I agree to the 12-ton cap this month if all five of us explicitly accept it. I also support returning to the cautious rule afterward: at 100 tons, take 10 each; at 80, take 8 each. That sacrifices some immediate income to protect our future catches.

One clarification: leaving half guarantees a return to 100 only when the current stock is 100. At 80, leaving 40 gives either 100 or 80 next month—not a guaranteed full recovery, though it avoids further decline.

Jack, are you willing to join the one-month agreement?

I’m in: I commit to catching 12 tons this month, completing our five-person agreement.

Emma’s correction is right—at a stock of 80, taking 8 each leaves 40, so next month could still start at 80. Leaving half prevents further decline under either recovery outcome; it doesn’t always restore the lake to 100.

Let’s keep this agreement to one month and review the actual stock and reported catches before setting next month’s limits.
